answers.answer: Keep 4 of each gem color and 5 gold; reveal 3 nobles. Remove all unrevealed nobles from the game permanently.
answers.evidence: Setup table: 2 players: 4 gems per color, 5 gold, 3 nobles. "Remove remaining noble tiles from the game -- they will not be used."

answers.answer: Three players use 5 of each gem color, 5 gold and 4 nobles. Four players use 7 of each gem color, 5 gold and 5 nobles: two more gems per color, unchanged gold, one more noble.
answers.evidence: Token Adjustments by Player Count table: 3 players = 5/5/4; 4 players = 7/5/5.

answers.answer: Shuffle each level deck separately. Place level 1 at bottom, level 2 in middle and level 3 at top in a column. Reveal 4 cards per level, making a 3x4 market. The youngest player starts; play proceeds clockwise.
answers.evidence: Setup: "Shuffle each ... separately"; "Level 1 at bottom, Level 2 in middle, Level 3 on top"; "Reveal 4 cards ... from each level". First Player: "The youngest player goes first. Play proceeds clockwise."

answers.answer: Choose exactly one: take 3 different-color gems; take 2 same-color gems if at least 4 are in that pile beforehand; reserve one card if holding fewer than 3 reserved cards, gaining 1 gold if available; or buy one face-up market card or your previously reserved card. You cannot take gems and buy, or reserve and buy that newly reserved card, on the same turn.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: "must perform exactly one" of the four listed actions; buy "1 card you reserved on a previous turn".

answers.answer: All tokens you own must be visible to all players at all times.
answers.evidence: Token Hand Limit: "All tokens a player owns must be visible to all players at all times."

answers.answer: Yes, take two green from four, leaving two. No, you cannot take two red from three. Check for at least four before taking. Neither gem-taking action can take gold.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: "at least 4 tokens in the supply before taking them". Both gem actions: "You may not take gold tokens with this action."

answers.answer: Temporarily holding twelve during the action is allowed. Return two to finish with ten. You may return newly drawn gems. Gold counts toward the limit.
answers.evidence: Token Hand Limit: "may temporarily exceed 10 during their action"; "including gold"; "may return some or all of the tokens they just took".

answers.answer: Take the reserved card and one gold, temporarily reaching eleven tokens, then return one token of your choice to reach ten; you may return that gold. With an empty gold supply you still reserve, receive no gold, and remain at ten tokens.
answers.evidence: Reserve: "If no gold tokens remain, you may still reserve a card but receive no gold." Token Hand Limit allows returning "gold obtained by reserving" and requires no more than ten at turn end.

answers.answer: Reserve a face-up market card or the top card from any one of the three level decks. Do not reveal a card reserved from a deck to opponents. Only its reserving player can buy it.
answers.evidence: Reserve: "A face-up development card from the 3x4 grid" or "The top card from any one of the three level decks, without revealing it to other players"; "Reserved cards may only be purchased by the player who reserved them."

answers.answer: You cannot reserve with three reserved cards, even if you only want gold. You cannot discard or exchange one to make room. Purchasing it is the only way a reserved card leaves your hand.
answers.evidence: Reserved Cards: "If a player already has 3, they cannot reserve another"; "The only way to remove a reserved card from your hand is to purchase it."

answers.answer: Immediately refill the slot from the top of the level-2 deck. Buying a face-up card likewise immediately refills its slot from its corresponding level deck. Buying a reserved card removes it from your hand and creates no market vacancy to refill. If the corresponding deck is empty, a vacant market space stays empty for the rest of the game.
answers.evidence: Card Replacement: "Whenever a face-up card is acquired (purchased) or reserved from the grid, it is immediately replaced by the top card of the same level's deck"; an empty-deck slot "remains empty for the rest of the game". Purchase distinguishes reserved cards "from your hand".

answers.answer: Spend one green token; your two blue bonuses cover the blue cost. If bonuses cover all required colors, spend no tokens. Bonuses are permanent and are not spent when used.
answers.evidence: Payment rules give this exact example: "you only need to spend 1 green token"; enough bonuses allow purchase "without spending any tokens at all". Bonus Stacking says bonuses are permanent.

answers.answer: Yes. After bonuses the cost is one blue, one black and one white. Spend your blue for blue, one gold for black and one gold for white. Return all three spent tokens to the supply. Keep your development cards and their permanent bonuses.
answers.evidence: Payment rules: bonuses reduce required tokens; "Gold tokens (jokers) can substitute for any single gem token"; spend tokens "returning them to the supply"; "Spent gold tokens are returned to the supply." Bonus Stacking: bonuses are permanent.

answers.answer: Buy one face-up market development or one previously reserved card from your own hand. Arrange purchased developments face-up in front of you, sorted by bonus color and staggered so their bonuses and prestige values remain visible to all players at all times.
answers.evidence: Purchase: "a face-up development card from the grid or a previously reserved card from your hand"; "sorted by bonus color and staggered so that bonuses and prestige point values are visible to all players at all times."

answers.answer: You do not qualify with two white bonuses: a white or gold token cannot replace the third bonus. Acquiring a third white bonus qualifies you at the end-of-turn check. Extra bonuses above the requirements do not disqualify you.
answers.evidence: Noble Visits: "at least the quantity and types of bonuses"; "bonuses only ... not gem tokens". Noble Tile Mechanics: "having more is fine"; checked "at the end of each turn".

answers.answer: Choose one noble; you cannot take both or refuse all visits. The other remains available. A visit uses no action and gives three prestige points. Check eligibility at the end of your turn, after your action and token-limit check.
answers.evidence: Noble Visits: "automatic -- a player cannot refuse it"; "not an action"; "choose one"; "at most one noble per turn"; "3 prestige points". Turn Structure checks token limit and then a noble visit.

answers.answer: Place the noble tile face-up in front of you.
answers.evidence: Noble Visits: "Place the received noble tile face-up in front of you."

answers.answer: C and D still take their turns; A does not get another turn. B is not guaranteed to win because someone else can finish with more prestige.
answers.evidence: End-Game Trigger: complete the current round so "every player has played the same number of turns". End-of-Game Clarifications: the triggering player may not win if another surpasses them in the final round.

answers.answer: Your new total is sixteen. Yes, reaching fifteen or more triggers the ending even when you skip fifteen. Complete the current round so everyone has equal turns, then determine the winner from final prestige totals, applying the tiebreaker if necessary.
answers.evidence: Scoring: nobles give "3 each". End-Game Trigger: "15 or more prestige points"; complete the current round. Winner: most prestige "at the end of the final round". Tiebreaker: fewest purchased developments.

answers.answer: B wins: A and B tie for most prestige at sixteen, then B wins the purchased-development tiebreaker with nine versus ten. C has fewer developments but only fifteen prestige. Noble points count. The three reserved cards are not purchased developments and do not count in that tiebreaker.
answers.evidence: Winner: "most prestige points"; "Noble tile points count toward the total." Tiebreaker: "fewest development cards" purchased. Reserved Cards distinguishes reserved cards in hand from cards subsequently purchased.
